summary: Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, the 13th Dalai Lama studied under Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, Tertön Sogyal, Lobsang Lungtok Tenzin Thinley, Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, Jampa Gyatso, Ngawang Pelden Chokyi Gyeltsen, and Yeshe Chopel.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, the 14th Dalai Lama studied under teachers including Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, and Tagdrag Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: In Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga and at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He held posts at Rizong Monastery, Drepung Loseling Monastery (1984), and Gyume Tantric College (1995–2008).

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Drepung Monastery (~1951–1959). He served at Central School for Tibetans, Shimla (1960), Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970), and as head of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Ayu Khandro.
He studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1908–1911). He later worked at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).
An Indologist, he was a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and japanology, Muller studied at Stony Brook, Virginia, Dayton, SCCC, and Kansai Gaidai under Sung-Bae Park and others. He held posts at Toyo Gakuen, Tokyo, Academy of Korean Studies, and Musashino University.
Working in Indology and religious studies, A. G. Mohan studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1971 to 1989. He founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

A philosopher educated at Jesus College, Cambridge, he taught at Swansea, Malta, Beaumont College, and Cardiff. He was Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972) and held appointments at Manhattanville University and Dalhousie University.

Specializing in philosophy and history/archaeology, Sabra studied at Alexandria University, University of London, and the London School of Economics under Karl Popper (~1950–1955). He held posts at the Warburg Institute (1962–1972) and Harvard University (1972–1996).

In Indology and linguistics, Ramanujan studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Indiana University Bloomington. He taught at MS University of Baroda, Deccan College, Harvard, and spent much of his career as a professor at the University of Chicago (1962–1993).
Working in Indology and philosophy, A. Mahadeva Sastri served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

An Indologist who studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar, he served as joint editor for Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

Working in linguistics and Indology, Narasimhia earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.
Active in Buddhist studies and Indology, Aggamahāpaṇḍita A. P. Buddhadatta was a member of the Kalyanavamsa Nikaya (attested 1923) and worked as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College.
Specializing in Indology and history/archaeology, A. S. Gadre served as Director of Archaeology for Baroda State and its Archaeology Department (attested 1944).
